newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-booking pulls Delhi shares to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-booking pulls Delhi shares to lower close.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) closed modestly lower on profit taking by speculators and local financial institutions, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 4.36 points lower at 738.89.
"Market remained depressed on persistent selling by speculators in the absence of buying by financial institutions," said Ajit Sial of brokers Sial and Company.
Brokers said market had lost the momentum build up after last week's upsurge triggered by cuts in lending rates by banks which is seen boosting liquidity for Indian industry.
Reliance Industries lost 1.70 rupees at 210.50 on sustained selling by speculators, traders said.
TELCO closed 7.50 rupees lower at 427, after touching a mid-session low of 418, they said.
ACC shed 28.0 rupees to close at 1,540.
State Bank of India bucked the trend to close 1.75 rupees higher at 234.0 on selective buying, brokers said.
